counterexamples.observed: A valid left-associated arithmetic expression succeeded at 900 operators but compile_ir failed around 1200 with Python RecursionError in recursive type inference.
counterexamples.fix: Replace expression type inference and C expression rendering with explicit iterative postorder machines.

counterexamples.observed: A 140-function acyclic call chain was accepted by the compiler but eval_function failed at the fixed RECURSION_LIMIT despite no recursive cycle.
counterexamples.fix: Keep recursive cycles compile-time rejected, but evaluate function/call/expression tasks with an explicit stack and make call-graph cycle detection iterative.

counterexamples.observed: lower_c(entry=None) emitted every function static; compiling the generated translation unit with -Werror -c failed as unused-function.
counterexamples.fix: No-entry/module lowering emits externally visible ccf_* functions; entry executables retain private static call-closure lowering.

counterexamples.observed: Emoji JSON escaping produced surrogate universal-character sequences rejected by GCC; embedded NUL also produced an invalid C universal character.
counterexamples.fix: Validate Unicode scalar strings, encode valid source strings as explicit UTF-8 octal byte escapes for C11, support String CLI parameters, and fail explicitly on the current const-char backend limitation C11_STRING_NUL_UNSUPPORTED rather than silently truncating.

validation.v16_frontend_discriminator: 69/69 PASS; strict lexer collision proof still requires interegular on target/current-main
validation.string_utf8_cli_and_content: 8/8 targeted cases PASS: ASCII, umlaut, emoji, newline, String CLI eq/ne, explicit NUL rejection, invalid surrogate rejection

epistemic_limits.known_open_string_gap: Embedded NUL is explicitly rejected by the current const-char C backend. A future length-aware runtime string representation may close this if BASE general-purpose acceptance requires arbitrary byte-containing strings.
